issues.title: Wrapper box model: the margin transfer deletes the 11px gap and the backdrop is 6px taller than the textarea
issues.detail: Measured in Chrome 151 against the real style.css, running Task 1 Step 4's attachMentionHighlight verbatim on a faithful reproduction of index.html:225-227: pane.top -> textarea.top goes from 11px (today) to 0px, pane height 171 -> 160, and backdrop.height - textarea.height = +6px. Two causes. (1) The textarea is display:inline-block (UA default, measured), so its inline style="margin-top:11px" never collapses today; moving it onto a BLOCK wrapper makes it a collapsible block margin that escapes through .source-pane (which has no CSS rule at all, hence no border/padding) and .field, then merges with the preceding sibling's margin-bottom:18px as max(18,11)=18 -- the 11px vanishes and the prompt box plus everything below moves up 11px. (2) Because the textarea stays inline-block inside the wrapper, the wrapper's line box adds a ~6px strut descender (body font-size:14px/line-height:1.5), so .ta-hl-back{inset:0} paints background:var(--field) -- and #fff under :focus-within -- as a 6px band with its own 14px radius sticking out below the textarea's rounded border. Glyph alignment itself is fine (backdrop.top - textarea.top = 0, measured). The plan's rationale is also wrong in both directions: inline-block margins do not collapse, and a margin that DID collapse through the wrapper would move the wrapper's padding box down with the textarea, so inset:0 would still align. FIX: make the wrapper's box exactly the textarea's box, e.g. `.ta-hl{position:relative;display:inline-block;width:100%;vertical-align:top;}` plus `.ta-hl > textarea.textarea{display:block;}` -- measured to restore the 11px gap and make backdrop.height - textarea.height = 0; that still leaves the pane 6px shorter than today, so finish with a measured check. Also replace the Task 1 test `assert.equal(ta.parentNode.style.marginTop, '11px')`: it asserts the implementation detail that causes the regression and passes while the gap is gone. jsdom cannot see the gap, so make it a Task 4 Step 7 browser check: the prompt box and every field below it must sit exactly where they do on master.
issues.location: Task 1 Step 4 (attachMentionHighlight margin-transfer loop) + Task 1 Step 3 (.ta-hl / .ta-hl-back CSS); spec 3.1 'Margin transfer'

issues.title: The scrollbar gutter goes stale on every geometry change that is not a repaint, and a stale gutter is a whole-line wrap divergence
issues.detail: syncMentionGutter runs only from repaintMentionHighlight, which runs only from `input`, the four programmatic hooks and the two reveal hooks -- nothing re-measures on a pure geometry change. Measured cost of being wrong by the 10px ::-webkit-scrollbar on a wrapped prompt: ta.scrollHeight 404 vs back.scrollHeight 383, i.e. a FULL 21px line, not a sub-pixel nudge; with the gutter padding applied both read 404. Every mention past the first divergent wrap point then paints blue on the wrong characters until the next keystroke. Real triggers that fire no `input`: dragging the resize:vertical grip shorter until content overflows (a scrollbar appears); window resize, including crossing @media (max-width:1080px) where .sidebar{display:none} widens the column; Poppins swapping in (font-display:swap, style.css:4-7) -- alignment is safe because both layers share var(--sans) and reflow together, but the line count changes so a scrollbar can appear or vanish; browser zoom. The plan's Architecture claim 'resize-drag and reflow need no observers' is true for the wrapper's SIZE and false for the GUTTER. FIX: add a geometry-only refresh that never rescans -- window.addEventListener('resize', ...) plus a `typeof ResizeObserver === 'function'`-guarded observer per textarea, both calling syncMentionGutter + syncMentionScroll. The typeof guard is value-based, so it satisfies the plan's own jsdom constraint. Add to Task 4 Step 7: drag the grip shorter until a scrollbar appears -- the colours must not shift. (Checked and dismissed as non-gaps: #source-seg plugin buttons wrapping and <details id="advanced-config"> opening change vertical position only, never the textarea width; autofill does not apply to textareas; undo/redo, cut, text drag-and-drop into the textarea and IME commit all fire `input`; both programmatic .value writers are hooked.)
issues.location: Task 4 Step 4 (syncMentionGutter) + the plan's Architecture paragraph; spec 5 'Scroll and metrics sync'

issues.title: Forced-colors / Windows High Contrast paints both layers' text at once and erases the blue
issues.detail: Measured with Emulation.setEmulatedMedia {forced-colors: active} in Chrome 151 under the plan's exact CSS: the textarea's color is forced from `transparent` to rgb(0,0,0) while its background-color stays rgba(255,255,255,0), and the backdrop's background becomes opaque rgb(255,255,255); .mention-ok's var(--blue-ink) is forced to rgb(0,0,0). So in High Contrast Mode both copies of the prompt text paint on top of each other (double-struck text, and any future sub-pixel drift doubles visibly) and the feature's only signal disappears -- in the app's primary input. The spec's justification ('There is no dark theme in this codebase ... so one palette suffices') conflates theming with forced-colors; prefers-color-scheme and forced-colors are unrelated media features. FIX: add one block to Task 1 Step 3 opting the two-layer trick out entirely -- `@media (forced-colors: active){ .ta-hl-back{display:none;} .ta-hl > textarea.textarea, .ta-hl > textarea.textarea:focus{color:CanvasText;background:Canvas;} }` -- and note it in the Task 4 Step 7 checklist. The rest of the accessibility story is sound: aria-hidden="true" on the backdrop plus an untouched focusable textarea means AT reads .value exactly as today, and caret-color:var(--ink) keeps the caret visible.
issues.location: Task 1 Step 3 (.ta-hl CSS block); spec 3.2 'Visual contract'

issues.title: Two of the four TDD 'verify it fails' states are wrong
issues.detail: Task 2 Step 2 says '3 PASS (Task 1's), 9 FAIL'. With `const marks = []` still hard-coded, four of the nine new tests assert deepEqual(blues(window), []) and therefore already pass: 'an @ that does not start a word is not a mention', 'a mention must end on a boundary', 'matching is case-sensitive', 'with no attached files nothing is highlighted'. True red state: 7 PASS / 5 FAIL. Task 3 Step 2 says '12 PASS, 6 FAIL' and names one already-green test, but 'a pasted prompt is validated on arrival' is also already green -- its only trigger is `input` (wired in Task 1) and rebuildMentionIndex is wired in Task 2 Step 5. True red state: 14 PASS / 5 FAIL. Task 1 Step 2 and Task 4 Step 2 are correct as written (all three Task 1 tests fail; the XSS and no-churn tests do pass early, as claimed). This matters because the executor is told to verify a specific red state, and a mismatch invites 'fixing' a non-bug. FIX: correct both counts and name the already-green tests, exactly as Task 3 already does for 'the markdown textarea highlights on its own input too'; and note that a negative assertion can never be red-first (those four are still falsifiable -- a too-greedy scanner breaks them -- they just do not drive the implementation).

issues.title: Two of the five hooks and the idempotency guard are asserted nowhere, and the Self-Review overstates coverage
issues.detail:
The syncSourceToggle hook (Task 3 Step 4d) and the showView('new') hook (Task 3 Step 4e) are added with no test at all, yet both are observable in jsdom: attach a file, type a mention into #promptMarkdown while its pane is hidden, remove the pill, then flip the source radio (or route to 'new') and assert the backdrop is correct. attachMentionHighlight's `if (ta._mentionHl) return` idempotency guard is likewise untested. Separately, the Self-Review claims 'Section 10 tests 1-19 ... all 19 present. No gaps.' -- spec test 19 is 'backdrop is a single text node', which the mandatory trailing
makes false; the plan silently substitutes a different assertion. FIX: add tests for 4d and 4e, and state the spec-19 deviation rather than claiming full coverage. (The one deviation the plan does declare -- dropping the hidden-pane gate -- is well argued and correct. Also fine as-is: 'a pasted prompt is validated on arrival' cannot really paste because jsdom cannot mutate a textarea from a ClipboardEvent, so value-set + `input` is the honest model; adding inputType:'insertFromPaste' would document the intent at zero cost. syncMentionScroll and syncMentionGutter are correctly left to the browser step, since jsdom pins scrollTop/offsetWidth to 0.)
issues.location: Task 3 Step 4d/4e, Task 1 Step 4 (idempotency guard), Self-Review 'Spec coverage' table

issues.title: The `sig` short-circuit allocates a full copy of the prompt to decide to do nothing
issues.detail: `const sig = `${marks.join(',')}|${text}`` builds a fresh 20,000-char string plus a joined marks string on every repaint, including the ones that short-circuit -- so the comment 'cost one string compare and touch no DOM' is not quite what happens. Keeping st.text and st.marksKey separately and comparing `text !== st.text` first is strictly cheaper and identical in effect. Practically this is sub-millisecond, so it is polish -- but it slightly undercuts a plan whose headline requirement is performance. For the record the scan itself is fine: I ran scanMentions verbatim and the worst case at the 20,000-char cap with 50 attached names all sharing one first-character bucket is 0.85 ms/scan (pure-@ 19,999 chars: 0.26 ms; realistic prose with 340 mentions: 0.11 ms), coalesced to once per frame; replaceChildren node counts stay under ~13k even for pathological input, well inside engine spread limits.

issues.title: Turn the 'no metric-affecting property may differ' constraint into a runtime check
issues.detail: The Global Constraints list nine properties and reads as exhaustive; the real set is about twenty -- it omits tab-size, text-indent, word-spacing, direction, text-align, hyphens, word-break, font-variant, font-style, text-rendering and font-kerning. I verified in Chrome that all of them already match between #prompt and .ta-hl-back under the plan's CSS, because parity comes from the shared rule at style.css:276 plus the shared inheritance chain (the textarea's UA `font: -webkit-small-control` shorthand resets exactly family/size/weight/style/variant/line-height, each of which the shared rule or the plan's block re-specifies) -- not from the enumerated list. But a future `.textarea{letter-spacing:-.01em}` would drift the two layers with nothing to catch it. Reframe the constraint that way and add one line to Task 4 Step 7: with wrapped text, ta.scrollHeight must equal back.scrollHeight. That single equality is a perfect drift detector -- it reads 404 vs 383 the moment one metric diverges, which is exactly how the scrollbar gutter shows up.

issues.title: mentionIndex.maxLen is dead weight
issues.detail: maxLen is only ever read as `if (!maxLen) return marks`, i.e. as 'are any files attached' -- byFirstChar.size says the same thing. Either drop it from the index shape (and from the spec's index type), or use it for a real early-out such as `if (text.length - i - 1 < shortestNameLength) continue` inside the scan loop.

summary: Strong, unusually well-grounded plan: every file:line citation checks out, the validity engine is correct on all nine boundary/greedy/case cases, initialisation ordering is safe as claimed, the .value submit surface really is closed, and the scanner benchmarks at 0.85 ms worst case at the 20k cap. Blocking on three defects that jsdom structurally cannot catch and that I measured in headless Chrome against the real style.css: the wrapper's margin transfer deletes the 11px gap and leaves the backdrop 6px taller than the textarea; the scrollbar gutter goes stale on resize-drag/window-resize/font-swap and a stale gutter misaligns a whole line; and forced-colors mode paints both layers' text at once while erasing the blue. Two minor issues (wrong TDD red states in Tasks 2-3; two hooks and the idempotency guard untested) round it out.
